**The meaning of the verse**
﴿وَلَا تَمْشِ فِي الْأَرْضِ مَرَحًا ۖ إِنَّكَ لَن تَخْرِقَ الْأَرْضَ وَلَن تَبْلُغَ الْجِبَالَ طُولًا﴾
And do not walk on the earth proudly and arrogantly; for you will never tear open the earth by walking on it like this, and you will never reach the mountains in height with your vanity, boasting and arrogance.

With the same meaning is the saying of Allah the Exalted in Luqman's advice to his son: Do not turn your face away from people when you speak to them or they speak to you, out of contempt for them and arrogance towards them, and do not walk on the earth among people proudly and haughtily. Allah does not love anyone who is arrogant and boastful in himself, his appearance and his speech. Be humble in your walk, and lower your voice and do not raise it.

And in the description of the servants of the Most Merciful: The righteous servants of the Most Merciful walk on the earth calmly and humbly, and when ignorant, foolish people address them with harm, they answer them with good words and speak to them in a way that keeps them safe from sin and from answering the ignorant with ignorance.

📖 At-Tafsir Al-Muyassar — King Fahd Complex.

**Talk with your child**
1. Why did Mazin not see Uncle Awad when he passed him in the alley, and not say salam to him?
2. What did Mazin see when he stood beneath the mountain? And why did he feel ashamed when there was no one with him to see him?
3. Is wearing new clothes and being happy with them arrogance? (No; Allah is beautiful and loves beauty. As in the story: there was nothing wrong with the robe; what was wrong was the way he walked. Arrogance is seeing yourself above people, so you look down on them and do not even see them.)

**This week's exercise**
This week your child is the first to say salam to everyone they meet, young or old, and every day helps someone without being asked, just as Mazin carried Uncle Awad's bundle. In the evening they tell you whom they helped.
